chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he was asked about the poor and the needy, so he said:
The poor is the one who does not ask, and the needy is the one who is more straitened than him, the one who asks.

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two (referring to the 5th or 6th Imam).
key_terms.الْفَقِيرُ: The poor; defined here as one who does not ask.
key_terms.وَالْمِسْكِينُ: The needy; defined here as one who is more straitened and asks.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a faqir and a miskin in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between 'faqir' and 'miskin' by linking the former to dignified self-sufficiency and the latter to active neediness. This differentiation is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining eligibility and distribution of Zakat, emphasizing that the 'poor' are those who do not beg, while the 'needy' are those in greater straits who do. The narration underscores the value of dignity in poverty, a key theme in Shia ethical teachings.
